`src/nl_shell/session_terminal.py:46-49`: the alternate-screen check only matches the three sequences as single parameters, so a multi-parameter DECSET (a "set private mode" sequence that sets several modes at once, which xterm accepts) gets past it and the alternate-screen output is captured. Reproduced: `printf 'A
\033[?1049;25hSECRET1\033[?1049;25lB
'; printf '\033[?25;1049hSECRET2\033[?25;1049lC
'` returned `result.text` with `SECRET1` and `SECRET2` in it. This does follow the letter of the new §6.2 text (`docs/design/specs/pty-protocol/v1.md` §6.2 names the literal sequences), so the gap is in the spec as much as in the code. A human should decide whether §6.2 means "mode 1049/47/1047 set by any `CSI ? Pm h`" (then the regex should parse the parameter list, and probably 8-bit CSI `\x9b` too) or only the literal forms. It is rare in practice (most TUIs send `\x1b[?1049h` on its own), but it is a concrete capture leak.

**The decision-6 drain rests on a race the brief calls a guarantee.** The brief says: "Because nl-shell forwards nothing after `D`, nothing new can arrive between the drain and readline starting." But bash writes `D` to fd 3 (`docs/design/specs/pty-protocol/v1.md:63`) and then starts draining at once. nl-shell only stops forwarding after it has *read and parsed* `D`. So the gap is bash's write → nl-shell's read, which takes time, and while that runs the forwarder can still write bytes to the session master. Any such byte that lands after the drain's "short" `-t` timeout runs out goes to readline. The next bracketed paste is then appended to it. Two problems follow. (1) Test (d) depends on timing, so it can be flaky under CI load, especially with the 200 KB burst still being forwarded when `D` arrives. (2) If it happens, the command that runs differs from the one the user confirmed. That is **Critical** in `.oss-scanner/threat_model.md:199`. The brief needs one of two things. Option A: a real ordering argument, e.g. the drain waits for a signal from nl-shell that it has stopped forwarding. This conflicts with §5.3 "Nothing else may be sent" (`v1.md:124`), so the brief would have to say how. Option B: state the residual race openly and give the human a decision on it at sign-off. Right now the human is asked to "confirm this mechanism" while the brief claims a guarantee it doesn't have.

**The drain's timeout is unspecified, but it adds a fixed delay to every prompt.** `read -r -s -N <k> -t <short>` runs at every prompt, including the first snapshot (seq 0) and every command that has no terminal attached, such as #140/#141's own tests. "<short>" has no value. It is a direct trade-off against the race above: shorter means a bigger race window, longer means slower prompts and a risk of hitting the timeouts in #140/#141's tests. The brief should pin the value, or a rule for picking it, and add a criterion that it doesn't affect #140/#141's tests or their timing.

**"Builtins only" does not cover a user's `read` function.** The rcfile sources `~/.bashrc` before installing the hooks (`v1.md:44,53`). A user function named `read` would therefore replace the drain without any error, and decision 6 would fail. The brief should require `builtin read`. A disabled builtin (`enable -n read`, which the `B` snapshot record tracks, `v1.md:92-93`) should be named as a case that sends the session to degraded mode or is otherwise accepted.

**The dependency is unbuilt and the brief's own text still contradicts itself.** `dependency-state.json` shows `141` exists with state `PLANNED`, not built. The brief has `Depends on: 141` (line 7), but plan-review response (2) still says "`Depends on: 101` puts this in wave 2 … with 101 built" (line 18). Falsifiability and Citations still say the verify base is "the folded branch with child-1" / "child-1 folded onto `main`" (lines 5, 14). After the split that is #140+#141. Two things need checking. (a) The driver must fold #140 transitively through #141, or else declare `Depends on: 140, 141`. (b) #141 (tamper checks) edits the same prompt hook. If it checksums the hook function's body (the brief can't know, since #141 isn't built), adding the drain will trigger #141's own tamper check and put every session in degraded mode. The brief should name this interaction and say whether #141's checksum must include the drain.

**The decision record can't be checked from this bundle.** The decisions that matter most (6, 7, and the 2026-10-15 human ordering) are cited only to `results/issue_10/brief.md:52-56` and `results/issue_10/notes.json`. This review received no `notes.json` and no `sources/`, only `brief.md` and `dependency-state.json`. The thread can't be compared with the brief. The human should confirm at sign-off that decisions 6/7 and "the strict pairing is this brief's reading" match what was actually decided. The brief is also changing normative spec text (§6.1 discard, §6.2 `?1047` and the pairing). That makes it a spec change, not only an implementation of the spec.

**The scope includes three normative doc edits as well as the feature.** These are the spec §1.3 reference rcfile, §6.1 and §6.2 (`v1.md:52-72,129-136`), plus ADR-0014 Decision 4's window ("From the start record", `docs/design/adr/0014-pty-session-protocol.md:62`). The brief chooses the spec over the ADR but leaves the ADR unchanged, so the two still disagree after the change. Either add a one-line ADR edit to the scope or record explicitly that the gap stays open. Otherwise Check will find the two docs disagreeing again.

**A small stale fact in the prior-art line.** It lists `src/nl_shell/` as "`__init__`, `__main__`, `cli`, `repl`, `router`". The target also has `src/nl_shell/input_modes.py`. This doesn't affect the plan, but the response says (9) "prior-art line corrected", and it still isn't.

T5 Judgment — Confirm decisions 6/7, strict alternate-mode pairing and the added bounded-loss mirror policy match intended scope; copying may drop output under backpressure, target/docs/design/specs/pty-protocol/v1.md:449. Also confirm affected-path merged and closed/rejected prior art: this target exposes only one synthetic base commit and no remotes, so the brief's prior-art claim cannot be independently settled here.
